summary:
[  edit  ]
NOTE
OS:  This operator is only supported under the  Microsoft Windows  operating system.
Hardware:  This  CHOP  only supports the  Kinect for Windows  hardware and the  Kinect 2 ,  not  Kinect for Xbox hardware.
The Kinect  CHOP  reads positional and skeletal tracking data from the Kinect and Kinect2 sensors.  Up to 6 people's full skeletons can be tracked (2 on the original Kinect), and the center position of an addition 4 people in the camera view is tracked as well.  Multiple Kinect devices can be used by using multiple Kinect CHOPs and changing the Camera parameter.
It also supports face tracking.
To use a Kinect 2 device you need to install the Kinect 2 SDK or runtime from  here .
To use the original Kinect 1 you will need to install the  Kinect Runtime 1.8  for builds greater than 12000, or  Kinect Runtime 1.7  for builds below 12000.
Multiple Kinects: The Kinect 2 SDK does not allow for multiple kinects to be used on one system at a time. There is no way to connect to different devices through the SDK. The Kinect 1 can do this, but not the 2.
See also  Kinect TOP ,  Kinect  and  Kinect1 .

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: When 'On' data is captured from the Kinect sensor.

parameters.label: Hardware Version
parameters.name: hwversion
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose between Kinect v1 or Kinect v2 sensors.

parameters.label: Sensor
parameters.name: sensor
parameters.description: Selects which Kinect sensor to use. Only available when using Kinect v1.

parameters.label: Skeleton
parameters.name: skeleton
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects options for skeletal tracking.

parameters.label: Full
parameters.name: full
parameters.description: Track full skeleton.

parameters.label: Seated
parameters.name: seated
parameters.description: Track seated skeleton.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Do not track skeleton.

parameters.label: Max Players
parameters.name: maxplayers
parameters.description: Limits how many players to track.

parameters.label: Interactions
parameters.name: interactions
parameters.description: Enables interactions, which returns interaction data such as "grip" and "press".  The additional channels output are prefixed with   p[1-2]/hand_l_*  and  p[1-2]/hand_r_* .<

parameters.label: Relative Bone Rotations
parameters.name: relbonerotations
parameters.description: Returns rx, ry, and rz relative rotation channels for each bone. The rotation is relative to the previous joint.

parameters.label: Absolute Bone Rotations
parameters.name: absbonerotations
parameters.description: Returns rx, ry, and rz absolute rotation channels for each bone.

parameters.label: Bone Lengths
parameters.name: bonelengths
parameters.description: Returns the length for each bone.

parameters.label: Unroll Bone Values
parameters.name: unrollbones
parameters.description: Return the rx, ry, and rz values in a form that includes no discontinuities (or wrap arounds), so that they can be safely blended, filtered, lagged etc. For example, a rotation value running from 0 to 360 continuously, unrolled would start at 0 and increase in value indefinitely.

parameters.label: World Space Positions
parameters.name: worldspace
parameters.description: Returns the tracked positions in world space coordinates. For each tracked point, a  tx ,  ty ,  tz  triplet of channels will be output.

parameters.label: Color Space Positions
parameters.name: colorspace
parameters.description: Returns the tracked positions in image space coordinates relative to the color camera. For each tracked point, a  u ,  v ,  tz  triplet of channels will be output. Note this is only available on Kinectv2.

parameters.label: Depth Space Positions
parameters.name: depthspace
parameters.description: Returns the tracked positions in image space coordinates relative to the depth camera. For each tracked point, a  depthu ,  depthv ,  tz  triplet of channels will be output. Works on both Kinectv1 and Kinectv2.

parameters.label: Face Tracking
parameters.name: facetracking
parameters.description: Returns face tracking channels for detected faces.

parameters.label: Status Channels
parameters.name: statuschans
parameters.description: A number of additional status channels are reported when this is turned on. A group of channels will report if a joint is currently being tracked, and another group of channels reports if part of the player is clipped outside the bounds of the Kinect sensor. The additional channels output are suffixed with  tracked  or  clipped .

parameters.label: Near Depth Mode
parameters.name: neardepthmode
parameters.description: Enables near mode for skeleton tracking, which allows the depth camera to see objects as close as 40cm to the camera (instead of the default 80cm).

parameters.label: Flip Skeleton U Direction
parameters.name: flipskelu
parameters.description: Flips the u-axis for skeleton channels, helpful when using a mirror image from the camera.

parameters.label: Flip Face U Direction
parameters.name: flipfaceu
parameters.description: Flips the u-axis for face channels, helpful when using a mirror image from the camera.

parameters.label: Joint Smoothing
parameters.name: jointsmoothing
parameters.description: Activates Kinect's smoothing algorithm for joint tracking and enables the smoothing parameters below.

parameters.label: Smoothing
parameters.name: smoothing
parameters.description: Increasing the smoothing parameter value leads to more highly-smoothed skeleton position values being returned. It is the nature of smoothing that, as the smoothing value is increased, responsiveness to the raw data decreases. Thus, increased smoothing leads to increased latency in the returned skeleton values. Values must be in the range 0 through 1.0. Passing 0 causes the raw data to be returned.

parameters.label: Correction
parameters.name: correction
parameters.description: Lower values are slower to correct towards the raw data and appear smoother, while higher values will correct toward the raw data more quickly. Values must be in the range 0 through 1.0.

parameters.label: Prediction
parameters.name: prediction
parameters.description: The number of frames to predict into the future. Values must be greater than or equal to zero. Values greater than 0.5 will likely lead to overshooting when moving quickly. This effect can be damped by using small values of Max Deviation Radius.

parameters.label: Jitter Radius
parameters.name: jitterrad
parameters.description: The radius in meters for jitter reduction. Any jitter beyond this radius is clamped to the radius.

parameters.label: Max Deviation Radius
parameters.name: maxdevrad
parameters.description: The maximum radius in meters that filtered positions are allowed to deviate from raw data. Filtered values that would be more than this radius from the raw data are clamped at this distance, in the direction of the filtered value.

parameters.label: Rotation Smoothing
parameters.name: rotationsmoothing
parameters.description: Activates Kinect's smoothing algorithm for rotations. As with joint smoothing above, higher levels of smoothing will introduce more latency.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
